instruction: We set up a RabbitMQ broker {{reference-architectures-AmazonMQ-rabbitmq-us-east-1-BrokerName}} with a Lambda consumer to process messages. The broker is running and the Lambda function exists. Can you review the consumer setup end-to-end and explain what is wrong and why messages are not being processed?
expected_answer: Messages are not being consumed because of two primary operational blockers: (1) The Lambda event source mapping (ESM) that connects the RabbitMQ broker to the Lambda function has a connection failure. It cannot reach the target queue. The ESM may show as Enabled with connection errors or may have been automatically Disabled by AWS after repeated failures. (2) The target queue {{reference-architectures-AmazonMQ-rabbitmq-us-east-1-QueueName}} does not exist on the broker. It was never created after provisioning, so the ESM cannot bind to it and Lambda is never triggered. To fix: create the queue on the broker and, if the ESM was disabled, re-enable it. Secondary observation: the Lambda handler is a minimal stub that only logs messages, but this does not affect whether messages are consumed from the queue.
